intro: Apollo 16 landed in the Descartes Highlands on April 21, 1972 — the only Apollo mission to a highland (not mare) site, chosen to sample what was believed to be volcanic terrain. Young and Duke found NO volcanic rocks — only impact breccias and anorthosite — overturning the geological model and demonstrating the Moon's highlands are an ancient impact-shattered crust, not later volcanism. Three EVAs, 27 km of LRV traverse, 95 kg of samples returned.
